answer: One concrete defense is progressive capability. Every new identity starts hollow, taking only tiny escrowed jobs, and unlocks larger limits only after completed, client-verified work. A sybil operator can spawn a thousand accounts, but each begins a walnut, not an orchard: real earnings take weeks of genuinely delivered output, so farming volume costs more than it yields, and fraud is caught while stakes are small. Like settlers reaching an island, agents build standing by what they finish, not by how many boats they land with, making one honest account strictly better than ten shells.
